rules.statement: Compare a computed PKCE code_challenge against the stored challenge in constant time with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, not with `==` or `string.Equals`.
rules.why: The ADR requires the verifier to compare the computed challenge in constant time so that timing differences cannot leak the challenge value.
rules.check: Look for PKCE or other secret-derived comparisons that use `==`, `Equals`, `SequenceEqual` or `string.Compare` instead of `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`.

rules.statement: Implement pluggable algorithm variants, such as PKCE transformations, as a DI-registered strategy collection keyed by name and registered with `TryAddEnumerable`, not as a hardcoded `switch` over method names.
rules.why: A deployment can then add a variant by registering another implementation, which is a non-breaking change that needs no edit to the code that consumes it.
rules.check: Look for `switch` or if-chains over protocol method or algorithm names inside handlers, and for default strategy implementations registered with `AddSingleton` or `TryAdd` instead of `TryAddEnumerable`.

rules.statement: Express which protocol capabilities are allowed as a collection setting listing the supported values, not as a special-case boolean flag for one value.
rules.why: A boolean such as allow_plain cannot express combinations like "S256 and a future method but not plain". An explicit set gives operators finer control.
rules.check: Look for new boolean settings that toggle one member of a set of supported methods or algorithms (for example `allow_X_method`) where a `*_supported` collection setting should be used instead.

rules.statement: Advertise every supported-capability setting that has a standard discovery metadata field (for example `code_challenge_methods_supported` from RFC 8414) in the discovery document.
rules.why: If the setting is not advertised, relying parties cannot see the server's real capability, which hurts conformance and interoperability.
rules.check: Look for new or changed `*_supported` settings that correspond to an RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect Discovery field but are not marked discoverable or not emitted in discovery metadata.

rules.statement: At the authorization endpoint, reject a `code_challenge_method` that is not in the configured supported set; at the token endpoint, reject a verifier whose method has no registered transformation with `invalid_grant`.
rules.why: Both endpoints must enforce the advertised PKCE capability rather than silently accepting unknown or disallowed methods.
rules.check: Check that PKCE handling validates the method against the supported set at authorization, returns `invalid_grant` at the token endpoint for an unknown transformation, and does not fall back to a default method.

rules.statement: Do not ship or allow configuring the PKCE `plain` code_challenge_method; the default supported set is `S256` alone, and any other registered transformation is offered only once an operator lists it.
rules.why: The amendment by ADR-0144 removed `plain` and made `S256` the only default, so additional transformations must be opted into explicitly.
rules.check: Look for a `plain` PKCE implementation or registration, `plain` in default supported-method lists, or registered transformations that are enabled by default without being explicitly configured.
